newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta harvest 90 to 95 percent done.
newsitem.headline: Alberta harvest 90 to 95 percent done.

text.p: Alberta's harvest was 90 to 95 percent done compared to 80 to 85 percent done last week, Alberta Agriculture said in a report for the week ended Nov 4.
The past weekend's snowfall brought harvesting to a halt. For some areas in northern Alberta five to 40 percent of wheat and canola will not be combined until spring.
If the ground freezes enough in the next few days and there is no new snowfall, farmers in the southern Peace River Valley could resume some harvest work, it said.
Southern and central Alberta completed their havest.
Northeast Alberta reported 95 percent of crops in the bin overall. The Athabasca district harvested 70 to 75 percent of crops, and Evansburg had 85 to 90 percent of crops in the bin.

Northeast Alberta reported 85 to 90 percent of crops in the bin in the Bonnyville district, 60 to 90 percent in Lac La Biche district, 70 to 75 percent in St. Paul district and 90 percent in the Vermillion district.
The Peace River Valley saw little harvest progress in the past week with 70 to 75 percent of the crop harvested. The southwest harvested 25 to 55 percent of crops.
Alberta Agriculture will issue its year in review Dec 9.
